Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed discrete random variables with probability mass function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the log-likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡L(\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i},\theta )) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(f({x}_{i},\theta )).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=3$ independent Poisson random variables with unknown parameter $\theta .$ Therefore, the probability mass function is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,\theta ) & ={e}^{-\theta }\cdot \frac{{\theta }^{x}}{x!}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can calculate the log-likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-\theta }\cdot \frac{{\theta }^{{x}_{i}}}{{x}_{i}!}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-\theta })+\operatorname{ln}⁡({\theta }^{{x}_{i}})-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{i}!) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(-\theta )+{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({\theta }^{{x}_{i}})-{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{i}!) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(-\theta )+{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\theta )-{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{i}!) \\  & =-\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}1+\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}-{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{i}!) \\  & =-n\theta +\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}-\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}!)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the sample data with $n=3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}! & =3!\cdot 3!\cdot 2!=6\cdot 6\cdot 2=72, \\ {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} & =3+3+2=8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, substituting the above values into our expression for $l(\theta ),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =-3\theta +8\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\operatorname{ln}⁡72.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
a+b+c=-3+8+72=77.
$$

Recall that if X1,X2,…,Xn are independent and identically distributed discrete random variables with probability mass function f(x;θ), where θ is an unknown parameter, then the log-likelihood function of a random sample x1,x2,…,xn is

l(θ)=ln⁡L(θ)=ln⁡(∏i=1nf(xi,θ))=∑i=1nln⁡(f(xi,θ)).

In our case, we are given a sample of n=3 independent Poisson random variables with unknown parameter θ. Therefore, the probability mass function is

f(x,θ)=e−θ⋅θxx!.

We can calculate the log-likelihood function as follows:

l(θ)=∑i=1nln⁡(e−θ⋅θxixi!)=∑i=1nln⁡(e−θ)+ln⁡(θxi)−ln⁡(xi!)=∑i=1n(−θ)+∑i=1nln⁡(θxi)−∑i=1nln⁡(xi!)=∑i=1n(−θ)+∑i=1nxiln⁡(θ)−∑i=1nln⁡(xi!)=−θ∑i=1n1+ln⁡θ∑i=1nxi−∑i=1nln⁡(xi!)=−nθ+ln⁡θ∑i=1nxi−ln⁡(∏i=1nxi!)

Now, using the sample data with n=3, we have

∏i=1nxi!=3!⋅3!⋅2!=6⋅6⋅2=72,∑i=1nxi=3+3+2=8.

Therefore, substituting the above values into our expression for l(θ), we get

l(θ)=−3θ+8ln⁡θ−ln⁡72.

Finally,

a+b+c=−3+8+72=77.
